name: Sugarcane
hook: Poor germination, gaps, uneven growth and worn-out soil.
intro: Sugarcane stays in the field for a year or more, and the same land often grows it again and again. Over decades this wears the soil out. Growers then see poor germination, gaps in the row, uneven growth and weak ratoons, even with new varieties and more fertilizer.
where: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh

product.name: Immunity Sugarcane Special
product.line: Made for sugarcane on tired soil: poor germination, gaps and uneven growth.

stages.name: Planting and germination
stages.text: Setts need moist, airy soil and healthy buds. Poor germination, sett rot and gaps show up here. Gaps filled late never catch up.

stages.name: Tillering
stages.text: The number of tillers decides the number of millable canes. Weak roots, compacted soil and early water stress reduce tillering.

stages.name: Grand growth
stages.text: Canes put on height and weight. The crop needs steady water and balanced nutrition. Lodging and pests matter most now.

stages.name: Maturity and ratoon
stages.text: Sugar builds up in the cane. After harvest, stubble care and soil health decide how good the ratoon will be.

problems: Soil hard and tired after years of sugarcane
More fertilizer every year for the same yield
checks: Get a soil test: organic carbon, pH and salts (EC) tell you a lot about tired land.
Use healthy, fresh setts from a good nursery.
Look at the roots of weak plants: are they short, brown or few?
Note where gaps are: low spots and hard patches point to water and soil structure problems.

faq.q: Why is my sugarcane germination poor?
faq.a: Common reasons are old or damaged setts, dry or waterlogged soil at planting, hard soil with little air, and sett rot. Tired soil with low organic matter makes all of these worse.

faq.q: Why does my sugarcane grow unevenly?
faq.a: Uneven growth usually follows uneven soil: hard patches, low spots that hold water, salts, or uneven irrigation. A soil test and a walk across the field at tillering show where the problem is.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for sugarcane?
faq.a: Immunity Sugarcane Special, developed with growers in South Gujarat. Immunity Granules can go in at planting for soil structure.

name: Potato
hook: Fewer, smaller tubers and rising fertilizer bills.
intro: Potato is a short, heavy-feeding crop. Many growers now use more fertilizer every season but get fewer tubers, smaller sizes and weaker skins. The cause is often below the ground: tired soil and weak roots at the moment tubers are forming.
where: Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Gujarat

product.name: Immunity Potato Special
product.line: Made for potato growers seeing fewer, smaller tubers and rising fertilizer bills.

stages.name: Planting and emergence
stages.text: Seed tubers sprout and roots start. Seed quality, soil moisture and soil temperature decide how evenly plants come up.

stages.name: Vegetative growth
stages.text: Leaves and stems build the plant's food factory. Strong roots now support more tubers later.

stages.name: Tuber initiation
stages.text: The plant decides how many tubers it will carry. Stress at this stage (water, heat, nutrient shortage) means fewer tubers.

stages.name: Bulking and maturity
stages.text: Tubers grow in size and weight, then the skin sets. Steady water and potash matter most.

problems: Yields falling on the same land
Fertilizer use going up every season
checks: Use certified, healthy seed tubers of the right size.
Test the soil before planting; potato land often has high salts or low organic carbon.
Avoid water stress at tuber initiation.
Dig a few plants at 7 to 8 weeks and count the tubers set.

faq.q: Why are my potatoes small?
faq.a: Small tubers usually come from stress during bulking: dry spells, heat, poor roots or a nutrient shortage. Too many tubers on a weak plant also stay small.

faq.q: Why are there fewer tubers per plant?
faq.a: The number of tubers is decided at tuber initiation, around 6 to 8 weeks. Stress at that time, weak roots or poor seed reduce it.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for potato?
faq.a: Immunity Potato Special, developed with growers in Punjab and Haryana.

name: Mango
hook: Tree decline, alternate bearing, fruit drop and small fruit.
intro: A mango tree is a long-term asset, and most problems build up over years. Growers bring us the same list: trees in decline, weak new growth, a good year followed by a poor one, flowers and fruit dropping, and small fruit.
where: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka and across India

product.name: Immunity Mango Special
product.line: Made for mango trees: decline, alternate bearing, fruit drop and small fruit.

stages.name: After harvest
stages.text: Pruning, cleaning and feeding the tree. New growth (flush) after harvest is next season's fruiting wood.

stages.name: Before flowering
stages.text: The tree needs mature shoots and stored food to flower well. Heavy late flush or stress now reduces flowering.

stages.name: Flowering and fruit set
stages.text: Weather, pests and the tree's reserves decide how many fruits set. Some drop is natural; heavy drop is not.

stages.name: Fruit growth
stages.text: Fruit size and quality need steady water and nutrition. Stress now causes late drop and small fruit.

problems: Small fruit, poor colour and taste
checks: Look at the root zone: is water standing, or is the soil hard and dry?
Check the trunk and branches for gummosis, borers and dieback.
Keep a record of each tree's yield year by year.
Test the soil every two to three years.

faq.q: Why do my mango trees bear fruit only every other year?
faq.a: After a heavy crop the tree has little stored food left, so it flowers poorly the next year. Good care after harvest, steady nutrition and the right pruning help even out bearing.

faq.q: Why are my mango fruits dropping?
faq.a: Some early drop is natural. Heavy drop follows stress: dry soil, hot winds, pests like hoppers, or a tree low on reserves.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for mango?
faq.a: Immunity Mango Special. Several thousand mango growers across India have used it.

name: Apple
hook: Plant mortality, root rot, low production and poor quality.
intro: Apple growers in the hills face trees dying in the orchard, low production and poor fruit, while costs rise every year. Many of these problems start in the root zone and build up over seasons.
where: Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir

product.name: Immunity Apple Special
product.line: Made for apple orchards: tree losses, low production and poor fruit quality.

stages.name: Dormancy
stages.text: Pruning, orchard cleaning and soil work. Chilling hours decide how well buds break in spring.

stages.name: Bud break and flowering
stages.text: Even bud break and good pollination set the crop. Frost and poor pollination reduce fruit set.

stages.name: Fruit growth
stages.text: Fruit size, colour and firmness build up. Water, balanced nutrition and leaf health matter most.

stages.name: After harvest
stages.text: The tree stores food for next year. Leaf health after harvest matters for next season's buds.

checks: Dig near a weak tree and look at the roots: healthy roots are white and firm, rotting roots are brown and soft.
Check drainage: water standing around trunks invites root rot.
Look at the collar (where trunk meets soil) for cankers.
Test the soil for pH and organic carbon.

faq.q: What causes root rot in apple trees?
faq.a: Root rot is caused by soil fungi that thrive in wet, poorly drained soil. Weak trees, injuries and old orchard soil raise the risk. See our apple root rot guide.

faq.q: Why are apple trees dying in my orchard?
faq.a: Common causes are root and collar rot, waterlogging, borers and replant problems. Find the cause before you treat; an expert visit helps.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for apple?
faq.a: Immunity Apple Special, developed for growers in Himachal Pradesh and Jammu and Kashmir.

name: Banana
hook: Wilt, leaf spot, plant losses and low bunch weight.
intro: Banana grows fast and feeds heavily. In Central Gujarat growers brought us wilt and leaf spot problems, plant losses and poor bunch weight. Soil health, clean planting material and balanced nutrition all matter.
where: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka

product.name: Immunity Banana Special
product.line: Made for banana: plant losses, weak growth and low bunch weight.

stages.name: Planting and establishment
stages.text: Disease-free suckers or tissue-culture plants and good drainage set the plantation up.

stages.name: Vegetative growth
stages.text: The plant builds leaves; the number of healthy leaves decides bunch size later.

stages.name: Shooting and bunch
stages.text: The bunch emerges and fills. Healthy leaves, water and potash matter most.

stages.name: Harvest
stages.text: Bunch weight and finger quality depend on how the plant was fed all season.

checks: Use disease-free planting material.
Look for yellowing that starts on older leaves and a split, discoloured stem, which point to wilt.
Remove badly spotted leaves.
Keep drainage good; banana hates standing water.

faq.q: What causes banana plants to wilt and die?
faq.a: Panama wilt is a soil-borne fungal disease that blocks the plant's water vessels. It spreads through infected suckers, soil and water. Clean planting material and healthy soil are the best defence.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for banana?
faq.a: Immunity Banana Special, developed with growers in Central Gujarat. Immunity Granules can go in at planting.

name: Citrus
hook: Dieback, fruit drop and weak roots.
intro: Citrus orchards (lemon, lime, sweet orange, mandarin) often suffer from dieback, where branches dry from the tip back, along with fruit drop and declining trees. Roots and drainage are usually where the trouble starts.
where: Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Punjab, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh

product.name: Immunity Citrus Special
product.line: Made for lemon, lime, orange and mosambi: dieback, fruit drop and weak trees.

stages.name: Flowering
stages.text: Water stress followed by irrigation triggers flowering. Even flowering gives an even crop.

stages.name: Fruit set
stages.text: Some drop is natural. Heavy drop follows stress or poor nutrition.

stages.name: Fruit growth
stages.text: Fruit size and juice need steady water and nutrition.

stages.name: Rest
stages.text: Pruning dead wood and feeding the tree for the next bahar.

checks: Check drainage and look at the roots.
Look for gummosis at the trunk base.
Check for zinc and iron shortage: yellow leaves with green veins.
Test soil pH; citrus struggles in very alkaline soil.

faq.q: What causes citrus dieback?
faq.a: Dieback has several causes: root rot and poor drainage, nutrient shortage, pests and old age. Treat the cause, not just the dry branches. See our citrus dieback guide.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for citrus?
faq.a: Immunity Citrus Special, with Immunity Granules for the soil.

name: Coconut
hook: Low nut yield, button shedding and weak palms.
intro: A coconut palm flowers every month, so its nutrition affects yield all year round. Low nut yield, button (young nut) shedding and weak palms are the problems growers ask about most.
where: Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and coastal Gujarat

product.name: Immunity Coconut Special
product.line: Made for coconut palms: low nut yield, button shedding and weak palms.

stages.name: Young palm
stages.text: Root and trunk growth. Good feeding now brings earlier bearing.

stages.name: Bearing palm
stages.text: A new spadix opens about every month. Nutrition today shows in nuts about a year later.

stages.name: Nut development
stages.text: Water and potash matter most for nut size and copra.

checks: Count nuts per palm per year to track yield.
Check the root zone: basins should hold water without standing for days.
Look for pests like rhinoceros beetle and red palm weevil.
Test the soil every two to three years.

faq.q: Why do young coconuts fall off?
faq.a: Button shedding follows water stress, poor pollination, pests or nutrient shortage, especially potash and boron.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for coconut?
faq.a: Immunity Coconut Special, with Immunity Granules in the basin.

name: Cotton

stages.name: Squaring

stages.name: Flowering and boll set

stages.name: Boll development

Watch for sucking pests in early growth.
Avoid water stress at flowering.

faq.a: Shedding follows stress: dry spells, waterlogging, heat, pests or nutrient shortage. The plant drops what it cannot feed.

name: Onion
hook: Small or uneven bulbs, weak roots and poor storage.
intro: Onion has a shallow, weak root system, so it depends on soil that stays loose and moist. Growers bring us small or uneven bulbs, leaf tips drying early and onions that rot in storage.
where: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat and Rajasthan

product.name: Immunity Onion Special
product.line: Made for onion: small bulbs, uneven size and poor storage.

stages.name: Nursery and transplanting
stages.text: Healthy, even seedlings and moist soil at transplanting give an even crop.

stages.name: Leaf growth
stages.text: Each healthy leaf adds a ring to the bulb. Leaf loss now means smaller bulbs.

stages.name: Bulbing
stages.text: Bulbs swell. Steady water and potash matter most; stop excess nitrogen.

stages.name: Maturity and curing
stages.text: Necks fall over. Good curing decides how long onions keep.

checks: Transplant healthy seedlings of even size.
Keep watering light and regular; avoid water stress at bulbing.
Stop irrigation before harvest so bulbs cure well.
Test the soil; onion dislikes salty soil.

faq.q: Why are my onions small?
faq.a: Small bulbs follow stress during leaf growth and bulbing: dry spells, weak roots, leaf disease or poor nutrition.

faq.q: Why do my onions rot in storage?
faq.a: Poor curing, harvesting too early, too much late nitrogen and bruising all shorten storage life.

faq.q: Which Immunity product is for onion?
faq.a: Immunity Onion Special.

Test the soil before sowing.
